title: Funk 'n Waffles
venue_description:
Funk 'n Waffles

Funk ‘n Waffles is a downtown Syracuse restaurant, bar and live music venue that has paired waffles with original and touring music since 2006. It was founded by then-Syracuse University students Adam Gold and Kyle Corea, whose late-night waffle-and-music parties grew into a full venue with a kitchen that runs deep into the night on show days. Gold’s own funk band, Sophistifunk, shaped the venue’s artist-first identity from the start.

Atmosphere and Setting

The room sits in the Armory Square area of downtown Syracuse, with restaurant-style seating that doubles as concert seating several nights a week. Venue staff have described the goal as building “a safe space to share their art judgment-free,” and that ethos shows in how the venue treats its recurring community nights — the tables clear for a headline act, but they're also where a nervous first-time open mic performer gets a warm reception.

Sunday Jazz Jam and Open Mic

Every Sunday afternoon from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM, Funk ‘n Waffles hosts a Jazz Jam built around a house rhythm section, giving improvisers of any level a chance to sit in. The room then turns over in the evening, from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM, for an all-genre open mic hosted by Attamizk & Friends that welcomes singer-songwriters, full bands, poets and first-timers alike. Both events are free to attend and sign-up happens in person at the venue.

Other Programming

Funk ‘n Waffles is also home to the monthly Sucka-Free Sundays hip hop showcase, run by promoter Ian LaRochelle, and hosts an annual MusicCares benefit open mic with guest performers. Outside of its community nights, the venue books a steady stream of touring indie, funk, hip hop and jam-band acts, making it one of the anchor stages of Syracuse’s original-music scene.

For Performers

Both the jazz jam and the open mic are drop-in, sign-up-in-person events, making them approachable for musicians new to Syracuse as well as regulars. The venue’s house PA and drum kit mean solo performers and full bands can both plug in without hauling their own backline.

Good to Know

Funk ‘n Waffles is located at 307-13 S Clinton St, Syracuse, NY 13202. Check the venue’s online events calendar for the current week’s lineup, since special ticketed shows occasionally take over the Sunday schedule.

title: Community Folk Art Center
venue_description:
Community Folk Art Center

The Community Folk Art Center (CFAC) is a gallery and cultural arts center affiliated with Syracuse University’s Department of African American Studies, dedicated to promoting and preserving the art of the African Diaspora. Located on East Genesee Street, the center pairs a public exhibition gallery with a Black Box Theatre used for performance, film and community events.

Atmosphere and Setting

CFAC reads as a community cultural hub first and a performance venue second — the Black Box Theatre is an intimate, flexible space rather than a traditional concert room, which suits the spoken-word-and-music format of its signature open mic. The center draws a mix of Syracuse University students, faculty and Syracuse residents, and its free-admission policy keeps the room accessible to first-time performers and audiences alike.

Snaps & Taps Open Mic Night

CFAC’s recurring open mic, Snaps & Taps, is held on selected Wednesday evenings from about 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM in the Black Box Theatre. It is free and open to the public, and welcomes poetry, spoken word and music in roughly equal measure. Hosting duties rotate among community artists — recent editions have been led by Randum and by Doclogik with guest performer Cheeki Williams — which keeps the night’s tone and format shifting slightly from month to month.

Other Programming

Beyond Snaps & Taps, CFAC runs a full calendar of gallery exhibitions, film screenings, gallery talks and studio classes covering disciplines such as dance and ceramics, reflecting its broader mission as a cultural institution for the Syracuse area.

For Performers

Because Snaps & Taps is free, all-ages and rotates hosts, it functions as one of the more low-pressure rooms in Syracuse for poets and musicians to try new material in front of a supportive crowd.

Good to Know

Community Folk Art Center is located at 805 E Genesee St, Syracuse, NY 13210. Since Snaps & Taps runs on selected Wednesdays rather than a fixed weekly schedule, check the Syracuse University events calendar or CFAC’s own listings to confirm the next date.

title: The Westcott Theater
venue_description:
The Westcott Theater

The Westcott Theater is a restored historic movie theater in Syracuse’s Westcott neighborhood, now operating as a live music venue in partnership with Fat Boy Pizza Co., which runs a full kitchen and bar inside the building. The pairing gives the theater a genuine neighborhood-hangout feel on show nights, with pizza and drinks flowing right up to the edge of the room.

Atmosphere and Setting

The theater retains much of its old cinema character — a proper stage, real sightlines and enough capacity to book regional and touring acts — while staying small enough to feel like a community room during its monthly open mic. It sits in the walkable Westcott neighborhood, a few blocks from the Westcott Street business strip.

Open Mic Wednesdays

On the first Wednesday of every month, the Westcott turns its stage over to the community for Open Mic Wednesdays. Sign-ups run on a first-come, first-served basis starting at 6:00 PM, with the show beginning at 7:00 PM, giving performers — musicians, comedians, poets and anything else that fits the format — time to grab a slice from Fat Boy Pizza and settle in before their slot.

Other Programming

Outside the monthly open mic, The Westcott books a steady calendar of touring and regional acts spanning rock, hip hop, metal and indie music, making it one of Syracuse’s larger dedicated concert rooms outside of downtown proper.

For Performers

Because the open mic is monthly rather than weekly and has sold out in the past, arriving close to the 6:00 PM sign-up time is the best way to guarantee a slot.

Good to Know

The Westcott Theater is located at 524 Westcott St, Syracuse, NY 13210. Check the venue’s website for the exact date of the next Open Mic Wednesdays, since the schedule can shift around holidays and touring bookings.
